 Search Go byu football Can No. 10 Cougars finally solve the Kansas riddle? 
 BYU puts its CFP hopes on the line Saturday in less-than-ideal conditions in Kansas against the explosive and upset-minded Jayhawks 
 Published: Nov 20, 2026, 3:45 p.m. MST See More Deseret News Stories In Search View 6 Comments Share BYU Cougars head coach Kalani Sitake walks the sideline during game against the Baylor Bears, Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026, at LaVell Edwards Stadium in Provo.  Cougars on the air
 No. 10 BYU (8-2, 5-2) at Kansas (4-6, 2-5)
 Saturday, 10 a.m. MST
 At David Booth Kansas Memorial Stadium
 TV: ABC
 Radio: 102.7 FM  / 1160 AM
 Cloudier conditions, cooler temperatures and perhaps a light drizzle early turning into a 55% chance of thunderstorms in the afternoon could ruin the string of perfect days in the northeast quadrant of the Sunflower State, just as the surging Jayhawks attempt to wreck the Cougars’ hopes of making it to the College Football Playoff and/or the Big 12 championship game. 
 Kickoff is at 10 a.m. MST and the pivotal Big 12 game will be televised nationally by ABC.
 Going off the teams’ records, it would appear that BYU (8-2, 5-2) should be a heavy favorite over somewhat disappointing Kansas (4-6, 2-5), until one takes a closer look at the Jayhawks’ talent level, performance against other top Big 12 teams, and history against the Cougars.
 For instance, the Jayhawks are 3-0 all-time against BYU, 2-0 in Big 12 games, and are the only team in the entire conference that the Cougars have never defeated. In BYU’s first-ever Big 12 game, Kansas got two defensive touchdowns and a big game from Jalon Daniels to edge the Cougars 38-27 in front of 47,233 in Lawrence.
 Two years later, the Jayhawks ruined undefeated BYU’s perfect season with a 17-13 upset in Provo, a devastating setback for the then-No. 6 Cougars that kept them out of the CFP and the Big 12 championship game. 
 Related BYU assistant coach says Kansas is best 4-6 football team he's ever seen How to watch Saturday's BYU-Kansas game “I remember it was a rough start (in 2023),” BYU coach Kalani Sitake said Monday. “I liked our start this past week against Baylor better. So, it was a rough start. It’s not easy to go out on the road, especially in conference games. We know we have to have our minds right, and make sure that everybody is clicking.”
 One particular player that needs to be clicking for the Cougars is senior running back LJ Martin , who is creeping closer to full strength after having played sparingly the past two games — the 28-20 loss at No. 2 Utah and the 28-7 victory over the Bears last week at LaVell Edwards Stadium.
 “They’ve competed with every single team they’ve played. This is the best 4-6 team I’ve ever seen (with) the type of talent they have on their offense. It’s very impressive.”
 —   BYU defensive coordinator Kelly Poppinga on the Kansas Jayhawks “I just know that he gets a little better each day and each week and (Tuesday) was the best he’s looked since he’s been back,” BYU offensive coordinator Aaron Roderick said. “So I wouldn’t say he’s 100% yet, but he looked good.”
 Quarterback Bear Bachmeier has been forced to carry more than his share of the load in Martin’s absence, but on Monday he said he’s “feeling good” physically and “in a good place” with two ultra-important games remaining in the regular season. 
 Kansas quarterback Isaiah Marshall, a redshirt sophomore, is also playing his best football of the season. The dual-threat QB reminds the Cougars of Utah QB Devon Dampier, and everybody in Utah knows what happened on Nov. 7 in Salt Lake City.
 “They can throw the ball and do a lot of different things that way, and spread you out,” Sitake said. 
 “But they can also pack it in and pound the rock, too. So that makes them really difficult to defend.”
 Kansas Jayhawks quarterback Isaiah Marshall (8) is wrapped up at the goal line by Utah Utes safety Rabbit Evans (1) during a game at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. | Lukas Katilius, Deseret News For BYU to win a football game in the state of Kansas for the first time in its 100-plus-year history, Bachmeier will need to take care of the football and outplay the opposing QB — something he didn’t do well at Utah. He bounced back against Baylor, accounting for four touchdowns and 158 total yards of offense with no turnovers.
 Bachmeier and Marshall are the only underclassmen in the nation to lead their teams in both rushing yards and passing yards. Only Texas’ Sam Ehlinger and TCU’s Max Duggan have done that in the Big 12 in the past 15 years.
 The Jayhawks are 16th in the country in rushing offense and 60th in passing offense. They are 38th in total defense. If there is a reason why they have lost six games, it is turnovers. They are 112th in the country in turnover margin (-5).
 Related Is this the best cornerbacks room in BYU history? “We’re gonna have to play our best game to be able to come out with a victory and be able to control their offense,” said BYU defensive coordinator Kelly Poppinga. “… They’ve competed with every single team they’ve played. This is the best 4-6 team I’ve ever seen (with) the type of talent they have on their offense. It’s very impressive.”
 6 Comments While Bachmeier struggled to pass the football in the rain at TCU, at least one BYU defender is hoping for inclement weather at The Booth.
 “Yeah, it’s ideal for us,” said linebacker Jake Clifton, a former Kansas State player. “I hope these guys come out in long sleeves. I hope they come out in fancy gloves and stuff that they haven’t done before. Because some people get into the mindset of, ‘I have a routine, and if it is raining, that messes my whole routine up.’ So it is going to be exciting. When we saw that there was going to be (bad) weather, that’s on our side, right?”
 An early start time — 11 a.m. local time — would seemingly favor the homestanding Jayhawks as well, but the Cougars say they will be ready, having gotten accustomed to it two weeks ago at Utah. Of course, the Cougars fell behind 14-0 in the first quarter against the Utes before recovering to take a 20-14 halftime lead.
 “We’re going to be fine with the schedule and the plan we have for the entire week,” Sitake said Monday. “… We’ll be ready. Our body clocks will be fine by the time the kickoff happens out there.”
